chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who vowed to give a large amount of wealth in charity, he said: 'A large amount is eighty and what exceeds it,' due to the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: 'Certainly, Allah assisted you in many places' [9:25], and they were eighty places.
ai.seo_question: What is the defined quantity for 'many' in a vow of charity according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines 'many' (kathir) in charitable vows as eighty units, deriving the number from the Quranic phrase 'many places' (mawatin) in Surah Al-Anfal. This interpretation reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking linguistic quantifiers to specific numerical values through Quranic exegesis, providing clarity for legal obligations. The hadith underscores the importance of precise definitions in fiqh to ensure vows are fulfilled according to divine precedent.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hussain Sa’d-Abadi, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said

with regards to a man who swore an oath to give an abundance of money as charity. He said: An abundance is eighty and what is above, due to the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: «Certainly, Allah assisted you in many places» [9:25] and they were eighty places.
